title: Zamzam, again
hookLine: pilgrims drink Zamzam, for whatever purpose it is drunk (Ibn Majah)

lines: FOR WHATEVER IT IS DRUNK FOR.
cards: A glass of water, and a question before you drink it: what is this for? On an ordinary day, the question never comes up. Thirst, habit, the meeting running long.
But a hadith in the collection of Ibn Majah makes it matter. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is reported to have said that the water of Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for. Not just thirst.
Whatever the drinker brings to it. You met this well back on day forty. Today it comes back, in the middle of the pilgrimage, with a new job.

teach.b: First, where the water comes from. Zamzam is a well inside the sacred mosque in Mecca, close to the Ka'ba.

In a long report in Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas tells how it first appeared: a mother alone in a dry valley with her baby, searching, and water breaking out of the ground. Her search is tomorrow's story.
Second, the Prophet at the well. Jabir's account of the pilgrimage, in Sahih Muslim, has him coming to the people of his own clan as they drew water at Zamzam and gave it out.
They handed him a bucket, and he drank. Ibn Abbas adds, in Bukhari, that he was the one who gave the Prophet Zamzam, and that the Prophet drank it standing. A man, a bucket, a crowd, a drink.
Third, the hadith from Ibn Majah. Some pilgrims take it literally.

teach.h: FOR WHATEVER IT IS DRUNK FOR.
teach.b: They stand by the taps and fountains, and before they drink, or while they drink, they ask for something. Healing for someone at home. Knowledge.
Forgiveness. A child. Some carry bottles of it home for the people who couldn't come.

Scholars have discussed the grading of this hadith, and readers take it in different ways; the habit it has formed is easy to see at the fountains. Fourth, what changes. Nothing about the glass is different.

teach.h: A REFLEX TURNED INTO A REQUEST.
teach.b: What changes is that the drinker stops, names a purpose, and turns a reflex into a request.

how: Pilgrims drink Zamzam water in the sacred mosque, often making a du'a before drinking, and some bring containers of it home to share with family and friends.

o: a spring pilgrims bathe in to wash away their sins
the well by the Ka'ba whose water is drunk with a hope
a river outside Mecca where pilgrims gather to pray

p: for whatever it is drunk for
drawing water and giving it out

s: the hadith says Zamzam is only for thirst
it says the water is for whatever it is drunk for.
in Jabir's account, the Prophet drank from a bucket at Zamzam
his clan was drawing water there, and they handed him a bucket (Sahih Muslim).
Zamzam is a river outside Mecca
it's a well inside the sacred mosque, near the Ka'ba.

games.q: you're a pilgrim at the Zamzam fountains with a cup in your hand. what do you do first?
o: name a purpose, make a request, then drink.
games.why: the hadith says the water is for whatever it is drunk for, so pilgrims name what they're asking for before they drink.

practice: Hold a glass of ordinary water, if you have one, and before you drink, name one thing you hope for, for yourself or for someone else, plainly and quietly.
If you pray, make it a du'a in your own words and say bismillah; if not, just name the hope. Then drink slowly.

wordCard.voice: Zamzam. The well beside the Ka'ba, whose water, the hadith says, is for whatever it is drunk for. Today's word.

orig.note: the name of the well beside the Ka'ba.

carryVoice: Your line: drink with intention. The water stays the same; the drinker changes. Until tomorrow.
